messages:
maria.prd: quick PRD draft for structured output + tool-calling. need a fast review before EOD Fri. TL;DR: define schema contract, validation behavior (strict vs lenient), error codes, fallback semantics, and launch metrics. grabbing the key acceptance criteria below — please react or reply with objections. :eyes:

alex.backend: quick q — are we validating at ingress (api gateway) or after model output parse? that affects latency and where the error codes are surfaced.

maria.prd: good q. proposal: validate after parse in the inference layer so we can map to model-specific errors, but provide an optional pre-parse lint check for user-submitted schemas. default behavior = strict (reject invalid outputs) for hosted; configurable lenient mode for Dedicated/Private.

sam.eng: runtime note: strict validation must be asynchronous-friendly. we should never block the main token stream for >1 sync validation call. implement synchronous fast-path (JSON Schema v7 subset) + async background checks for expensive rules. if async check fails, emit a regression alert and metric, but don’t impact user response.

kate.qe: adding test concerns: streaming outputs may be truncated by model — how do we treat partial JSON? Accept partial and attempt recovery or treat as invalid? we need deterministic rules for QA.

maria.prd: proposed rule: for streaming responses, the service will attempt incremental accumulation and parse once a balanced JSON object/array is observed. if stream ends without balanced payload -> fallback to raw text output + validation error code VMTR-01. include heuristics to auto-close common truncation patterns (unclosed braces) as opt-in (nice-to-have).

alex.backend: draft schema example (for clarity):
```json
{
  "response_type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "action": {"type":"string"},
    "payload": {"type":"object","properties":{"query":{"type":"string"}}}
  },
  "required":["action"]
}
```
We should require `action` be one of allowed tool names in registry. validation must enforce whitelist.

sam.eng: think about tool auth: tool calls must include `tool_context` with caller tenant id and signature, and the runtime must check permission before executing. if permission denied -> return structured error with code TOOL-AUTH-403 and do NOT execute. Also sanitize args to avoid injection.

kate.qe: QA checklist items (short):
- missing required field -> invalid + no execution
- extra unknown fields -> by default ignore, but flag in debug logs
- wrong type -> invalid
- nested arrays with >1000 items -> soft-limit -> reject with PAGIN-01
- streaming truncated -> VMTR-01
- tool permission denied -> TOOL-AUTH-403
- validator regression test harness + fuzzing

maria.prd: acceptance criteria (MUST):
- schema v1 defined and documented (JSON Schema v7 subset)
- validator integrated in inference pipeline with deterministic error codes
- fallback behaviour: when strict validation fails, response falls back to raw text + structured error metadata in response envelope
- tool calls must include `name`, `args` and `signature` fields; name must map to registered tool
- launch behind feature flag with canary rollout (10% customers)
- measurable metrics: %valid_responses, fallback_rate, tool_auth_fail_rate, p95_latency_diff

AC (SHOULD / NICE-TO-HAVE):
- auto-correct heuristics for common truncation (opt-in)
- developer debug endpoint to replay failing outputs with original model context
- example SDK helpers for schema generation and client-side preflight validation

OOS (out of scope):
- binary attachments, streaming multi-chunk schema stitching across multiple responses, and custom non-JSON encodings.

alex.backend: one more perf constraint: strict validation path MUST add <10ms median and <30ms p95 for typical payloads (<=2KB). fallback path (stringify) must be <50ms extra. we should measure across CPU profiles and list worst-case.

sam.eng: agreed. I'll add microbench harness. also config knob: `redwood.validate.verbosity = {strict, lenient, none}` for Dedicated/Private. Hosted default = strict.

kate.qe: I'll own the test matrix and add unit + integration tests. will include: schema conformance, streaming truncation scenarios, tool permission cases, error code mapping, and performance smoke tests. plan to start tomorrow.

dev-bot: docs preview deployed: https://staging.redwood.dev/docs/structured-output-v1 (preview link, internal only).

maria.prd: action items:
- alex.backend: finalize schema whitelist and validator integration plan (owner) — due Wed 11:59am
- sam.eng: perf harness + config knobs for lenient mode — due Thu EOD
- kate.qe: test matrix + initial test cases — due Thu EOD
- me (maria.prd): update PRD with acceptance list + rollout plan and post final by Fri noon.
React with :thumbsup: if you’re good or comment otherwise. will lock PRD Friday if no major objections.

alex.backend: :thumbsup:

sam.eng: :thumbsup:

kate.qe: a couple of minor notes — will post sample failing payloads in thread tomorrow.

maria.prd: great, thanks everyone. if you have edge-case examples now drop them here so I can fold into acceptance criteria.
